2026-12-02.title: Wednesday of the First Week of Advent
readings: The Lord will make a feast for all peoples
I shall live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life
Jesus heals many and feeds the multitude
2026-12-02.verse: I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way.
theo: Isaiah promises a mountain banquet for all peoples, rich food and fine wine, and more: God “will swallow up death forever” and “wipe away the tears from all faces”. In the Gospel that promise begins to come true on a mountain by the Sea of Galilee. Crowds bring the lame, the blind, the mute; Jesus heals them. Then, moved with compassion, he takes seven loaves and a few fish, gives thanks, breaks them and gives them to the disciples to distribute. All eat and are filled, with seven baskets left over.

The words “took, gave thanks, broke, gave” are the words of the Last Supper. Advent prepares us to receive the One who is Bread from heaven, born in Bethlehem, whose name means “house of bread”. And the disciples are his hands: Christ multiplies what we bring, but asks us to distribute it to the hungry.

2026-12-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, compassionate Shepherd, you healed the sick and fed the hungry on the mountain. Feed me with your Bread of life, and make my hands generous to those who have nothing to eat. Amen.
altar: The Mass is a foretaste of the banquet on the mountain of the Lord. The One who multiplied the loaves feeds us now with the Bread of Life.

quick: God promises a feast and the end of death.
Christ multiplies what we bring and asks us to share it.
2026-12-02.action: Give a meal or groceries to a needy family.
2026-12-02.question: Do I give thanks for my daily bread?

family.explain: Jesus felt sorry for the hungry people and fed them with only seven loaves. When we share the little we have, Jesus makes it enough.
family.intention: We pray for children and families who are hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone in need this Advent?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you had compassion on the hungry crowd. As we gather, heal our wounds, feed us with your word and teach us to share our bread. Amen.
share: Isaiah promises that God will wipe away every tear (Isaiah 25:8). What tears do I bring to the Lord today?
The disciples saw what they lacked; Jesus asked what they had. What ‘loaves’ can I offer?
Who around me is hungry, in body or in spirit?
pm.resp: Lord, have compassion on your people.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of healing and feeding for all peoples.
For the hungry and the poor, that they may find bread and dignity.
For the sick, the disabled and the suffering, that Christ may heal them.
For those who grieve, that God may wipe away their tears.
For our parish, that our Advent sharing may be generous.
pm.close: Lord God, you prepare a banquet for all peoples. Make us generous with the little we have, so that through us many may be fed, until we sit together at your table in the Kingdom. Amen.

illus: A parish in Kochi began collecting one packet of rice from each family every Advent Sunday. The first year they hoped for a hundred packets. They received over a thousand. A parishioner said: “We gave seven loaves; God made it four thousand.”

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah today describes a great banquet on the mountain of the Lord: a feast of rich food and well-aged wines for all peoples (Isaiah 25:6). It is a feast for all nations, not one people only. And at that feast God will destroy the shroud that covers all peoples; he will swallow up death forever and wipe away the tears from all faces (Isaiah 25:7–8).
This is the hope of Advent: not only a baby in a manger, but the final banquet of the Kingdom, where death is no more and every tear is wiped away. Christmas begins what that banquet will complete.

In the Gospel Jesus goes up a mountain by the Sea of Galilee. Great crowds come, bringing the lame, the blind, the mute and many others, and he heals them. Then he has compassion on the hungry crowd, and with seven loaves and a few fish he feeds four thousand. All ate and were filled, and seven baskets were left over (Matthew 15:29–37).

Notice the order: first Jesus heals, then he feeds. And notice his words: I have compassion for the crowd. Jesus sees physical hunger as well as spiritual hunger. Isaiah's mountain banquet is already beginning on the hillside in Galilee.

The disciples asked: where are we to get enough bread in the desert? They looked at what they lacked. Jesus asked: how many loaves have you? He looked at what they had. Advent invites us to give our little loaves to the Lord, our time, our money, our talents, and let him multiply them.

This Advent, let us feed someone who is hungry: a migrant worker, a poor family, a lonely person who needs company more than food. And at each Mass let us remember that we are already tasting the banquet of the Kingdom. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus fed thousands with just a few loaves. When you share even a little, Jesus can do great things with it!

intro: God promises a feast; Jesus heals and feeds; the Eucharist sends us to the hungry.

q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.

Then Jesus called his disciples to him and said, “I have compassion for the crowd, because they have been with me now for three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry, for they might faint on the way.”

sub: Jesus heals the lame, blind and mute.
God's promise is fulfilled in him.
Our sorrows are not the last word.
q: He will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces, and the disgrace of his people he will take away from all the earth, for the LORD has spoken.
He will wipe every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; mourning and crying and pain will be no more, for the first things have passed away.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who is grieving.

sub: The words of the Last Supper.
Christ is the Bread from Bethlehem.
q: The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want.

He took the seven loaves and the fish; and after giving thanks he broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds. And all of them ate and were filled; and they took up the broken pieces left over, seven baskets full.
points.apply: Say grace before every meal this Advent.

concl: Christ feeds us so that we may feed others.
The feast has begun at the altar.
